newsitem.title: POLAND: POLISH 1996 CPI SEEN AT 18 PCT,GDP UP AROUND 7 PCT.
newsitem.headline: POLISH 1996 CPI SEEN AT 18 PCT,GDP UP AROUND 7 PCT.

text.p: The Polish economy is likely to expand in 1996 by 6.7 to 7.0 percent and inflation should fall to about 18 percent from 21.6 percent last year, Finance Minister Grzegorz Kolodko told a news conference on Monday.
"Inflation at the end of the year will be about 18 percent while producer price inflation should be between 10 and 11 percent," Kolodko said.

"This year we will have 6.7 percent to seven percent growth (of gross domestic product). I hope that it will be closer to seven percent and next year I expect growth of more than six percent," he added.
The National Bank of Poland sees 1996 inflation at about 18.6 percent and analysts' predictions range between 18.5 percent and 19 percent.

The 1996 budget set a growth target at 5.5 percent but several analysts expect Poland to top this goal thanks to faster second half expansion fuelled by strong domestic investment and consumer demand.
Kolodko also said that 1996 budget deficit might fall below 2.4 percent of GDP against the planned 2.8 percent, but gave no further figures.
"I would risk a statement that this was the best year for the Polish economy," Kolodko said at conference summing up this year's economic achievements.
